title: BP Care: What Your Numbers Really Mean After 35

title: Does Heat Raise or Lower Blood Pressure? (Especially After 35)
description: Heat often *lowers* BP in healthy adults—but dehydration or meds can cause spikes up to 140/90. Learn what’s normal, when to worry, and how to stay safe this summer.
reasoning: Summer heatwaves are surging globally, triggering real-time concern among adults 35+ who notice erratic BP readings outdoors—especially those on medication or managing hypertension. Users aren’t seeking textbook physiology; they want actionable, age-relevant clarity on why their numbers shift in heat and whether it’s dangerous.
